claim: Let \(\psi\) be a continuous convex function on \([0,1]\) with \(\psi(0)=\psi(1)=1\), \(\max\{1-t,t\}\le \psi(t)\le1\), and \(\psi(t)=\psi(1-t)\). Let \(N_\psi\) be the associated absolute normalized norm on \(\mathbb R^2\), and put \(\psi_2(t)=\sqrt{(1-t)^2+t^2}\). If either (i) \(\psi\ge\psi_2\) and \(\psi/\psi_2\) attains its maximum at \(t=1/2\), or (ii) \(\psi\le\psi_2\) and \(\psi_2/\psi\) attains its maximum at \(t=1/2\), then the Ptolemy constant and Euclidean Banach--Mazur distance satisfy \(C_{\mathrm{Pt}}(N_\psi)=d_{\mathrm{BM}}((\mathbb R^2,N_\psi),\ell_2^2)^2\). In case (i) both equal \(2\psi(1/2)^2\); in case (ii) both equal \(1/(2\psi(1/2)^2)\).
integrity: The Ptolemy component is tied directly to Theorems 2.2 and 2.3 of the cited open-access primary source; the Banach--Mazur component is proved independently by finite-group averaging of arbitrary positive-definite quadratic forms.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to coordinate-symmetric absolute normalized plane norms with a one-sided Euclidean comparison whose relevant ratio is maximized at the midpoint. No claim is made outside that class.
title: Ptolemy constants equal squared Euclidean Banach--Mazur distortion for a symmetric absolute plane class
